page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-72 is an Arm-based cloud virtual machine tailored for compute-heavy infrastructure tasks. Built on the arm64 architecture, this machine type provisions 72 dedicated virtual cores paired with 144.0 GB of system memory. The configuration maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, allocating exactly 2.0 GB of memory per core.

Hardware resource allocation is stripped of extraneous accelerators and integrated disk storage. The instance features zero local storage, requiring attached persistent network storage for operational filesystems and state. Similarly, there are zero hardware GPUs included, and the configuration allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, targeting environments that operate within private cloud subnets.

The dense 72-core Arm implementation allows execution of large-scale parallel software with efficient instruction throughput. By constraining the allocation to 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, memory footprint costs are minimized for tasks that require high processor density rather than large in-memory caching capacity.

The c4a-highcpu-72 is aligned with compute-dominated applications where memory overhead is minimal. Suitable workloads include distributed batch processing, high-throughput web serving, continuous integration and compilation pipelines, and containerized microservice backends.
